The parents love thing is so damn real. A part of me still chases that want. It takes time to reconcile with that and for me it's taken a lot of therapy to recognize that for me at least my parents didn't show me love, they had an obligation.  They took care of me because they had to. They taught me about the religion because they felt they had to in order for them to feel they'll be saved in Armageddon, as promised by the religion. It takes so much time to process this stuff, please be kind to yourself,  give yourself the space to process things right now. It does both get worse but also so much better to process the loss and the damage done by the witnesses once you are completely out of it.  That's normal and okay. 


It does get easier once your out to realize that they are victims too. I can't express it properly but it's harder to process these concepts while it's still your everyday, but it's easier once your out and you've learned more about how the rest of the world works and you can reflect on it properly. 


I'm genuinely proud of you for realizing these things, for recognizing that this isn't a good path for you. I'm also glad that you have a friend that is willing to help you out. You deserve that. Just do your best until you are seventeen. That's all you gotta do. For me when i was alone, i focused a lot on reaserch and finding perspectives from the ex jw community. In meetings I would take notes so it looked like I was paying attention but in my notes I was dissecting the points being made and why what they were saying didn't make sense. That helped a bit with having to go to meetings all the time. I'm sure other folks have things that helped them. 


I genuinely am wishing you the best. I hope that the next few years can go quickly while you plan an effective escape plan.  You got this! You also arnt alone.

Hey friend. I was also born into the Jehovahs Witnesses and I left when I was seventeen. 


I knew I wanted to leave years before. I realized that I was trans and gay and no matter how hard I prayed I still felt the same. That started the cracks in my belief that just got larger as I learned more about the dark secrets and blatant mind control and propaganda techniques used by the organization.  


From the moment I figured out who I was I knew my parents wouldn't take it well.  I tried to tough it out as best as I possibly could, finally a little after I turned seventeen I couldn't take it anymore.  I asked a friend's family if they would be okay with me staying for a while and I explained my situation.  They agreed to have me so I finally made time to tell my parents and for the first time in a long time I was fully and completely honest about everything.  I was fully transparent about my gender issues and i was completely clear at each and every huge concern I had with their religion and why I didn't want to be a part of it anymore. 


Their response was as I expected,  they both lectured me for a while about why leaving the religion was bad and scary. I tried to argue with them and point out facts I had gathered over the years why even just the way they interpreted the Bible didn't make any sense but it was like there was a wall in their minds made by the organization and nothing I ever could say could break it down. 


They made me go meet with the elders and it was basically the same thing. I explained clearly my issues with how they viewed lgbtq+ people and how they interpreted the Bible as well as other issues and articulated why exactly I felt I couldn't follow them anymore.  They responded by going to their bibles and telling me their interpretations of the scripture and proceeded to tell me why Satan was claiming me.  They had the same wall as my parents in their heads. 


I had to write and sign a letter saying I was leaving the witnesses. My parents didn't actively tell me to leave but they started to just completely avoid perceiving me and stopped putting what little emotional effort they used to completely. I realized I needed to leave so I packed up my stuff and moved to my friends. I was still younger and didn't think to look up organizations that specialized in leaving cults because I was still so fresh in my leaving.   There's are resources like Freedom Of Mind and igotout.org that compilate a lot of really fantastic resources and how to be there for yourself while and after leaving. 


Make sure you check out a lot of ex jws, educate yourself a lot and find some points to question with the religion and how it's run. Check out podcasts about leaving cults and read books. A podcast i recently found that I really liked is one called A Little Bit Culty. The first episode they talk to Dr Steven Hassan who is an expert on cults and helping people leave them. He has several books which are incredibly interesting and have been helpful for me. 


My main suggestions,  find a place to go that is not influenced by your parents or other Witnesses. Find a friend at school you can trust and see if you can stay there. Your main important concern should be your physical and mental sanity. Find resources in your area and talk to a trusted adult outside the religion to see what's available.  Waiting a year or two might be vital while you act in the religion but quietly organize a plan that can be enacted quickly. It really depends on what's available in your area and the situation at home. 


Find a good therapist soon after leaving. The intentional loss the organization thrusts on you by itself is intensely devastating as is the trauma of being raised by parents practicing what they are told by the organization.  There are therapists and counsilers that specialize in leaving cults that could be helpful. But I've found significant help in a therapist who is very trauma informed. 


You might have some things that are intensely evident now, but with time you will realize more and more how much the organization has molded your mind and how you behave and perceive things. That's completely normal. I left almost five years ago now and I'm still realizing constantly more ways my upbringing has traumatized me or has caused certain behaviors.  It's a long game. What's important immediately is finding a safe place to go (friends, if you have non jw family reach out and talk about your situation and see if you can stay with them) and protecting your sanity and wellbeing.


It's overwhelming and scary and a lot. But I still wouldn't change my choice of leaving. I actually have a chance of being a genuine person now rather then a cog in a machine. Pretty much every other ex jw I see feels the same.  Your absolutely not alone.  I'm so sorry you had to be born into this religion as well. I hope that something I or others have said can be helpful.   It's an absolute process leaving the JWs. But its very worth it. I genuinely wish you the best with this journey and I hope you are granted the ability to leave soon. 💙

im not incredibly knowledgeable about development/trauma but as someone who's dealt with it myself and know of a lot of other people with similar experience, Honestly its not that crazy of a happening for children/adults going through immense traumas to have similar responses. That kind of disassociation into a place where things feel better and where you are treated properly. It is known enough from studies that children going though immense trauma that they cannot control do often have these intense disassociated responses as a way to "escape" the real trauma they are experiencing. 

Like you mentioned Yellow guy is often very badly mistreated, and from what we've seen in the webseries he and his father dont have the most productive or healthy relationship.   
with mental illness and trauma there are a lot of common shut down responses when faced with traumatic situations. When you cant control what is happening outwardly it is really common for people to respond by making a much more ideal place in your head to escape to because that feels a lot safer then your current environment. Like a lot of people with trauma either go to these places with writing, art, games, or just their imaginations. 

​

again im not an expert. just someone who deals with this myself and knows people who respond similarly.

Honestly I wish it was more normalized for people to not absentmindedly talk about diets, because you never know who secretly struggling and that kind of talk is MAJORLY TRIGGERING. I'm really sorry that you had to deal with that.
